name: Plotter on Ink
summary: A dark engineer's drawing board: a glowing orange pen spark plots every line and word as it is said; spoken-word karaoke (outline, signal wipe, bone), Archivo slams stepping through widths, deadpan technical annotation, HDR glow and grain.

palette.use: ink: the board, slightly warm black
ink2: raised panels, boxes, inset graphs
bone: primary text, said words, plotted lines, the grid
ash: unsaid-word outlines, notes, dimension text, axes
graphite: dim lines, secondary text, line numbers
signal (hazard orange): the spark, the word being said, carets, strikes, numbers
ember: the spark's ring and the first frames of a fresh stroke or slam
one rare accent for a single moment per video; never in these samples

type.case: UPPERCASE slams, spoken rows as written, spaced-caps labels
type.emphasis2: the voice: outline → signal wipe → bone

banned: hand-set keyframes: every move is a function of time keyed to a spoken word
cutting after a line's first word: cuts sit in the pause before it
off-palette colours (no light-blue grid; acid only once per video)
old-style figures in Cormorant (lining figures only)
relying on the ▸ and ⏎ glyphs in Plex Mono: draw them
a dark halo behind captions on paper
photos, footage or stock icons: everything is line, type and glow
decorative motion that no word triggers
pen fonts without a known licence (the source's Hershey/EMS single-stroke fonts are not used)

sources.what: Motion as Code workflow guide and its kit (the engine and style of pdoom-video)
